6. Mr. A. K. M Faiz, the learned advocate appearing for the complainant-petitioner submits that the learned Judge misread and misconstrued section 32 and fail to appreciate that the provision of the criminal amendment Act, 1958 applies except section 6(5) with regard to sanction and in view of section 4 of the criminal law Amendment Act, 1958 the learned Special Judge has Still wider jurisdiction to take cognizance of Case upon receiving complaint of fact.. which constitutes such offence or upon a report in writing of such fact which is not barred. As such the learned Senior Special Judge ought to have taken cognizance and Proceeded with the matter instead of dismissing the Special case summarily. Thu Earned advocate further submits that considering the provision of section 28(2) (3 ) read with section 4 of the criminal law Amendment Act, 1958 a private persons has no right to file a complaint before the commission. The learned advocate then submits that e en if bar to institution of case without previous sanction as provided under section 32(1) of the Ain is admitted no rule for determining the procedure for according sanction has been framed till date. As such the bar is not attracted in the instant case: 

 8. Perused the petition of complaint filed before the Senior Metropolitan Special Judge, Chittagong dated 14.03.2006 being numbered as Special case No.6 of 2006, and order No.1 dated 14.03.2006 passed by the learned Special Judge and the relevant of provision of Ain and heard the learned advocate and the learned Deputy Attorney General at length. The Durnity Daman Commission Ain, 2004 came in to force on and from 09 may 2004 by notification published by the Government in official gazette dated 09 May, 2004. 

 9. From comparative and analytical study of the law of Durnity Daman Commission Ain, 2004 briefly the Ain and provisions made there under reveal a complete departure from the previous dispensation. From the definitions of 'commission', means, Durnity Daman Commission established under section 3 'Commissioner' means Chairman of the commission or any other Commissioner; 'Chairman' means Chairman of the commission, "Tofsil" (Schedule) means Tofsil under the Ain, "Durnity" means offences mentioned in the schedule, "Nirdharita" (determined) means determined by rule, means rule framed under the Ain, "Sachib" (Secretary) means Secretary appointed under section 16 of the Ain, as provided in the definition clause under section (2) (ka) (kha) (ga) (gha) (Umma) (cha) (Niyaan) and (ta) respectively. Section 3 proclaims to establish a commission called "Durnity Daman Commission" (Anti-corruption commission) to achieve of the cherished object of the Ain which will be independent and neutral commission soon after enforcement of the Ain. Notably after formation of the commission by gazette notification dated 21.11.2004 under section 3 with power amongst others to frame rule with prior approval of the President as provided under section 34 and erstwhile .Bangladesh Bureau of Anti-corruption stood abolished with vesting of all assets right, power and privileges of the Government in the commission under section 35 of the Ain. Ongoing through the provision of section 17 we find the commission is empowered to carry out all or any of the acts, inter alia to enquire and investigate in to the offences, institute and conduct a case on the basis of enquiry and investigation and to institute an enquiry suo moto or on the basis of complaint of aggrieved person or filed by any person on his behalf and the commission is vested with special powers in regard to any enquiry and investigation to fulfill the object of law as specified in section 19. Under section 20 the commission alone is eligible for investigation of offences under the Ain and those mentioned in the schedule thereto and also the commission may empower any subordinate officer of the commission by gazette notification to conduct the investigation. Section 28(2) provides that all other provision of the Criminal Amendment Act, 1958 shall apply excepting section 6(5) and section 6(6) i.e. two provisions regarding previous sanction to obtain from the Government for prosecution of public servant and section 6(6) with regard appointment of public prosecutor are have been done away will and section 32 and there as the indispensability of the previous sanction of the commission as an independent and neutral body Section 28(3) provides that in case any provision of the Criminal law Amendment Act, 1958 appears inconsistent with the provision of the Ain, the provision of this Ain, shall prevail. 

 11. Mr. A. K. M. Foiz at one stage expressed grave concern and submits since sole authority for investigation of offences under the Ain and those mentioned in the schedule is vested with the commission and eventually no complaint under section 4 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 (Act 40 of 1958) can be instituted without previous sanction of the commission in view of the bar in section 32(1) though no rule for determination of procedure for according sanction by the commission has been framed till date a vacuum prevails and in the meantime an ordinary people or citizen victim of highhandedness and corruption of public servant will be left with no remedy because they have no access to the commission and such situation will encourage corruption to thrive with impunity than preventing it.
